A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AnyMC3D and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-H. Matching content across layout changes supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments across 12 tasks, with ablations, calibration experiments, and subgroup analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results and supplementary experiments, including Tables 2 and 4-8 and the calibration analysis.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same LoRA adaptation, query-based slice and view pooling, auxiliary segmentation objective, and heatmap generation. The redrawn Figure 2 illustrates the existing procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 12 CT/MRI tasks and datasets in Tables 1 and 3. Supplementary trauma-grade scenarios and other evaluated conditions are also retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark, task-specific comparisons, and appendix experiments. This includes PanDx, CT-Net, CT-CLIP, DeepCNTD, and the same adaptation and fusion alternatives.

E3.justification: Table 3 preserves the splits, sample counts, preprocessing, and input sizes. Training settings, calibration and ensembling procedures, and supplementary threshold selection are unchanged.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same decoder, adaptation, fusion, backbone-size, and DINO-version analyses, alongside data-regime tests, calibration comparisons, heatmap studies, and trauma subgroup analysis.

E5.justification: There are no changes to seed or repeated-run information, uncertainty estimates, or significance testing. Performance reporting remains based on point estimates and the same learning curves.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results and qualitative findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains average AUC 0.894 for both AnyMC3D (MII) and AnyMC3D (DINOv3); visual inspection confirms the same curves and calibration scores in Figures 7 and 9.

T1.justification: Equations 1-12 retain the same mathematical content, including the classification formulation, adaptation, pooling, segmentation objective, attention maps, and calibration. No formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about scalable adaptation, the 12-task benchmark, general-purpose versus medical FMs, and 2D versus 3D methods.

C2.justification: The limitations paragraph is shortened but preserves its substantive boundaries: evaluated FM coverage, unexplored modalities, costly segmentation labels, and potential dense-prediction applications. Result interpretations elsewhere remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendices A-C retain the same pseudocode, hyperparameters, augmentation, preprocessing, baseline implementation details, and access links. No new technical or resource-availability information is disclosed.

R1.justification: The same 67 works remain cited, with unchanged research positioning. References 9, 22, and 34 update existing Merlin, CT-CLIP/CT-RATE, and PanDx entries to publication versions; these are bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v2 corrects grammar and capitalization, condenses the limitations paragraph, updates bibliographic details, and replaces several appendix references to 'the main paper' with 'Sec. 4'. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn with descriptive panel headings, revised component symbols, and simplified flows. The anatomical illustration beside Table 1 is cleaned up, page numbers are added, and spacing and page breaks shift; the experimental displays retain their content.

improvement.justification: The explicitly labeled Figure 2 makes the framework and its extensions easier to follow, while copyediting, tighter limitations prose, and more precise cross-references improve readability. These are limited presentation gains; the methodology, empirical evidence, and substantive caveats are retained.
